title: We Love Magenta
slide_intent: Demonstrate how repeated, conspicuous color can become a recognition cue before a viewer reads a name.
strategic_value: Magenta across stores, events and venues can accumulate T-Mobile recognition across different encounters.
demonstration: A magenta text panel sits beside a collage of illuminated retail, branded activity, venue signage and crowds.
practical_value: Make magenta the visual lead and use black or white to balance it rather than letting accents compete.

content_islands.name: Color rationale and rules
content_islands.spec: Place the white title, explanation and four rules on the magenta left panel.

content_islands.name: Environmental color collage
content_islands.spec: Fill the remaining area with retail, event and venue examples separated by narrow magenta gutters.

ingredient.name: Magenta
ingredient.role: Signal T-Mobile through a dominant, repeatable color.
ingredient.application: Make magenta the hero; keep non-magenta elements near it, balance with black and white, and use tertiary colors sparingly.
ingredient.scope: Brand expressions covered by the February 2024 guide. Tertiary colors are primarily, rather than exclusively, for owned environments.

reference_purposes.Intent: The opening paragraph associates magenta with energy, excitement and immediate T-Mobile recognition.
reference_purposes.Expression: The collage shows magenta lighting, clothing, signs and crowds carrying one color across different physical settings.
reference_purposes.Application: The top rules direct designers to lead with magenta, keep other elements near it and use black and white for balance.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Tertiary colors are limited to sparse use, primarily in owned environments.
